beats.text: One morning, every house in town found a fresh loaf of bread on the doorstep.
Still warm. No note. No name.
The next morning, again. And the next.
Free bread. Every single day.
Nobody knew who was baking it.
People stopped going to the bakeries.
Why pay for bread when it shows up for free?
The first bakery closed after a month.
Then the second.
Then the third.
By spring, there was only one bakery left in town.
A small shop on Church Street, owned by a friendly old man named Mr. Crumb.
And then, one Monday morning, the doorsteps were empty.
No bread. Not that day. Not ever again.
So the whole town lined up at the only bakery left.
Mr. Crumb smiled, and raised his prices.
Double.
Then triple.
You see, the free bread was never free.
Mr. Crumb baked every single loaf himself, every night, in secret.
He lost money, every single day, for six whole months.
And now, he owns every slice of bread in town.
People in town still miss the mystery baker.
They have no idea they buy from him every morning.
